column10: Notes/Outlook
God Emperor Wemby is currently the MVP frontrunner. The league (and your leaguemates) should be terrified he's already this good.
More of the same from SGA as the reigning MVP. We know what to expect out of an elite performer and a unanimous top 2-3 dynasty pick in all formats.
Luka continued to show why he's an absolute superstar with the Lakers. As expected, a lot of sparks this year and especially as of late at the end of the year.
Jokic is still dominating at a high level. He's 31 now but his game will age like fine wine. Averaging anything close to a triple double is par for the course at this point.
Flagg has looked as advertised despite some normal rookie struggles and he'll keep getting better quickly. Expect him to remain a consensus top 5-10 player.
Cade has officially ascended last year and led the Pistons to the best record in the East. A collapsed lung will knock him out until the playoffs.
Maxey has been fantastic to start the year. I had doubts about him being a winning first option guy but he's truly there right now.
Ant continues to ascend so far beyond any of my expectations. He's had his best season to date and is averaging close to 50% FG and 40% 3PT on the year.
I can't deny Jalen Johnson any longer. He's emerged into a full-blown fantasy and IRL star this year.
Jayson Tatum is back on the court and quickly returning to form. He's back to my top 10 for next year when he's 100% again.
Cam Boozer looks the part of an elite-level fantasy basketball player with how he stuffs the stat sheets. He is the very obvious, "don't overthink it" 1.01.
Chet continues to be awesome for fantasy purposes and is having another fantastic year.
Haliburton suffered a devestating Achilles injury in game 7 of the NBA finals. I've bumped him up a bit in preparation for his return going into next year.
Alperen Sengun continues to grow and is having the best year of his young career. He has improved on both ends of the ball but the defense remains an issue.
JDub has had a down year due to his wrist and hamstring injuries. I'm buying the dip on him this offseason if people are starting to panic.
I think it's fair to say Mobley has been underwhelming this season after being great last year. Still in on him as a top-20 asset moving forward.
Barnes has continued to step it up in the fantasy game this year. He's been very efficient from the field even if the 3-point shooting isn't there.
There are sure to be questions about Giannis if he gets traded, but in most situations, he will remain a top-end fantasy contributor well through the end of his prime.
Peterson was once in the running for 1.01, but his hamstring injury has been a blemish on his season. I'm not concerned about the assists this year with Kansas.
Frankly, I've been a little disappointed by Amen Thompson relative to the expectations coming in. Still an elite player and asset to hold onto, though.
Reaves has stepped up in a big way this year and gotten better with him and Luka at the reins. He is a truly special talent and an incredible find by LA's front office.
Mitchell has had arguably his best Cavs season yet. He and James Harden have been a good pairing and I expect Mitchell to stay in Cleveland a while longer.
The entire Magic squad has struggled this year. I think they may be best suited with Wagner as their 1A, but his availability has been an issue this year.
Avdija is stamped as legit and he's Portland's best player moving forward. He gets his first All-Star nod this year. Not worried about his back.
That Dybantsa is somehow the 1.03 in any rookie draft is just absurd. He's a special talent not far off from Peterson in contention to go 2nd overall.
Trae Young gets moved to WAS to be their point guard of the present... and maybe the future, as they gear up to improve with him, Anthony Davis and the youngsters.
Booker is who he is by now and will continue putting up essentially the same numbers as always. The 3-pointers are tailing off to under 6 3PA.
Brunson is still playing well and in his prime, but it's clear that the drop-off could be coming sooner than later as a small guard.
Despite decreases in his points, Ball is still cruising and doing what he's best at. He's a high-level playmaker and has meshed really well with Kon Knueppel this year.
I'm still not the biggest fan of the Giddler, but I can't deny that he's been great for fantasy and this all is sustainable as Chicago's "franchise player".
Kon has been an important piece for Charlotte and has shown a way stronger fantasy profile than other dynasty creators thought. He's the frontrunner for ROTY over Flagg.
Harper has been fantastic starting out. I think it's clear by now that he, Fox and Castle can coexist for now, even if usage gets a little hairy.
After some initial struggles, Trey Murphy has rebounded and continues to deliver well off a career year.
Paolo has underwhelmed as a categories fantasy player, but he's started to have a better year compared to years' past.
Duren has stepped up this year and has a real chance at winning Most Improved Player. Defense remains an issue but he is DET's second best player by a long shot.
Sarr has taken some steps this year and has a cleaner profile for fantasy. He's playing well for still being 20, though he's now known as the guy Bam dropped 83 on.
Murray has been great so far this year as Denver's healthiest player on the roster. He gets his first All-Star appearance and has a good shot at All-NBA.
For some, the Big 3 of the 2026 Draft is actually a Big 4. Caleb Wilson has ridiculous potential as a super high-impact, two-way player and a possible fantasy star.
Garland's injury issues came to a head this year, and he was traded to the Clippers. He'll be their franchise point guard moving forward.
JJJ was shockingly traded to Utah in a blockbuster deal no one saw coming. He's a great compliment to Walker Kessler with two great defenders in the frontcourt.
Edgecombe has established himself as Philly's present and future as they aim to build with him, Maxey and Embiid.
It's obvious that a KAT trade may be brewing soon if the Knicks cannot win in the playoffs this year.
Bam Adebayo has been having a good year, but who could've seen him scoring 83 points for the 2nd all-time high in points?
Jaylen Brown has been real good as the leading man for the Celtics. He'll settle back into the prior role with Tatum now back.
Harper and Castle are making the conversation around Fox interesting. He feels very expendable as they'll start to assess payroll and getting Wemby a megadeal soon.
Flemings is set to be the 5th pick in real life and in dynasty drafts. He's got franchise point guard written all over him and has been a star for Houston.
Bane has remained at a high level even in Orlando. He's been their mainstay all year with plenty of injuries up and down the roster.
I'm not terribly worried about Lauri moving forward, either leaving via trade or with JJJ and Kessler in the frontcourt. Dude's just a good player.
Harden heads to Cleveland for another stint ended by money disputes. He's still doing his thing at a high level.
Sabonis got ravaged by injuries this year, and his future with the Kings and as a top-end fantasy player will remain a question mark.
KD has continued doing his thing, this time in Houston on a team full of youngsters. I expect about 1-2 more years at this level of play.
Steph Curry is still Steph Curry even at age 38, but there have been a lot of times he's looked human in recent years with his injuries. Hold and enjoy the ride.
It's been a weird year for Tyler Herro with his slew of toe injuries and other issues. He remains a higher-end, yet worrisome asset.
Davis was shockingly traded to Washington this February. He will remain out for the rest of the year, but he should be interesting to see play for this squad when healthy.
Brandon Miller has continued to have injuries and leaves some serious questions about him, LaMelo and Charlotte on the whole.
George has played with a real sense of urgency to make that leap this year. He's here and establishing he belongs as a longer term starter.
Zubac was traded to Indiana in a shocking move involving their first round pick this year with protections. It's obvious they value him highly.
Zach Edey is a potential fantasy monster when he's healthy and showed some amazing play for Memphis, but at his size, the injuries have been a concern.
Early returns have been nice on Castle and he's had a great second half of his season. He's got a very solid future ahead of him.
Despite shooting under 40% on the year, White has been ridiculously impactful as always for Boston.
Clingan has made leaps and bounds developmentally this year. If the 3-point shot continues at this level, he's a fantasy monster and will move into my top 50.
Okongwu retakes his full role with the Kristaps Porzingis experiment not working well. The 3-point shot has really emerged this year.
Siakam has been great for the Pacers as we expected. This year without Haliburton has been rough for the team but Siakam still plays at a high level.
Queen has flashed very, very high potential so far in his rookie season. The defense remains a concern, but I'm still bought in.
Some remarks by Spoelstra on Ware's effort and motor have me concerned about this issue dating back to college, but he has a lot of really strong potential.
Ja has really struggled badly this year and with drama brewing in Memphis, I want no part of him at cost even if he still mantains some value.
Zion has stayed relatively healthy, but he's had a bit of a down statistical year in general.
Wagler has been incredible this season. He has some concern areas and needs to put on more weight, but the higher-level outcomes are very exciting.
Kessler suffered a brutal season-ending injury just a few games in. Really tough situation for Utah, but it's clear they want him and JJJ for the present and future.
Daniels was a stocks god this past season and that's trailed off this year. Not been as good but he's still a good, impactful piece for ATL.
Suggs needs to stay healthy for Orlando to be at his best. Very impactful player on the whole.
We know what to expect with OG Anunoby at this point. He's clearly made his mark on the Knicks and is such a winning connective piece.
The Bulls' future is Buzelis' oyster now. Some brilliant flashes and more to come. There's a lot here to be excited about.
We've seen some good stuff out of Sheppard that remind us why he went so high in drafts, but the concerns are still there.
Hartenstein has recently been banged up with a hamstring sprain that's had him in and out. Very important player that OKC may get priced out of.
Kyrie was playing great until a devastating ACL tear. He was already approaching the end of his prime and this does leave some strong questions about the future.
Mikel Brown has the makings of another star fantasy guard. He's not without his concerns but the upside is very strong.
When he plays, he's an elite fantasy player. Will Kawhi ever play a normal regular season again? What will happen with his Aspiration scandal?
Jarrett Allen has been excellent since James Harden joined the Cavs about a month ago. Is he expendable moving forwrd?
George has absolutely early into the season, but he's slowed down in 2026 a bit. Expecting solid things from him.
As expected, Coward has been up and down, but the highs have been very exciting. I remain high on him moving forward.
A lot has changed for Utah from when Bailey was drafted to now. I expect him to take another jump next year after having a good stretch this year.
Ausar has continued to struggle progressing on offense. He's still got loads of great upside and is a fantastic defender.
Ingram has had a good year for Toronto where he's stayed very healthy. Nothing new with his numbers but his production remains strong at cost.
Mikal has had some bad play recently, but he is still a quality fantasy player who produces well for categories leagues.
Embiid is clearly not the guy he was in his last healthy season as the MVP, but he can still drop big numbers.
Quaintance has the makings of an elite NBA defender, but I need to see more on the offensive end. He may have limited potential if that doesn't improve.
Burries has played himself firmly into lottery status and possesses a lot of the winning, two-way traits you want to see in a long-term NBA starter.
Scoot missed a lot of the season and started out very slow. He's had some hit-or-miss performances since returning. Lot of questions about him moving forward.
McDaniels continues to flash fantasy upside as he gets better in this career year he's having. Great two-way player and is building up a reputation as an iron man.
As always, Quickley is streaky and can run hot or cold depending on the night, but he's locked into TOR for the long haul and playing well.
MPJ has been playing at an All-Star level this year even if some of it is pretty Mickey Mouse. He's going to be very important to Brooklyn's tank.
Acuff has been a straight-up star for Arkansas and there's no telling just how much further he can keep going. Concerns are obvious and there is a chance he's a bust.
Fears has been very solid for fantasy so far, which is really shocking considering we thought he would be bad for at least a year like normal rookie guards.
There is still a lingering possibility of a Nic Claxton trade, but he's been a mainstay for Brooklyn. Would love to see the 2+ blocks coincide with the increase in assists.
CMB has been brilliant in his best moments this season in Toronto. It's easy to see how he fits into this offense. Future All-Defense guy, for sure.
Eason hasn't been quite as good this year, but there has been an uptick from 3. Availability remains an issue.
I love the fit of Coby White as the 6th man in Charlotte. He's been ramping back up due to injury but his best moments so far in Charlotte are exciting.
Randle has mostly rebounded to his old self in Minny. Sometimes you get Julius Randle, sometimes you get Dubious Handle.
Rollins has had an awesome breakout year in Milwaukee. He's very clearly the best guard on the Bucks right now.
Black was on fire for a lot of this 3rd season that should get him some MIP votes. He's quieted down a little recently, but he's had a fantastic year on the whole.
I've been underwhelmed by Sharpe, who just doesn't possess much of a fantasy game besides scoring and hasn't played all that well relative to his high usage.
NAW has blossomed in Atlanta and looks like a pivotal piece, especially with Trae Young gone. He's up to 20.3 PPG on the year.
I've raised Murray a decent bit up here as he's coming back and looking OK following the Achilles tear. I'm skeptical still about his long-term outlook but deserves the bump.
More of the same for Mark Williams in Phoenix as he's taken a slight step back in the numbers on a winning team.
I think we know by now that LaVine is not super conducive to winning as a leading scorer, but the stats are stats all the same in a fantasy setting.
Smith's fantasy appeal is clear, but he's struggled with inconsistency. He's had stretches where he's impressed and disappointed me this year.
Poeltl had himself a career year and he finally got paid. This year, he's regressed a bit and the back stuff is concerning.
Pritchard struggled early in the year but is putting up some big shotmaking performances on a wide open Boston team.
To be fair, Green has been hurt for a majority of the year and been slow coming back from the hamstring... but he's been straight up bad numbers wise.
Turner has been pretty disappointing this year for Milwaukee. Will be interesting what the plan is with him if Giannis is traded.
I've been low on Keegan Murray for years. I just don't know that I buy him being much more than this. Clean stat profile, but nothing too exciting.
Like Bailey, Tre Johnson has a game more for points leagues. He's a solid shooter and I'm curious how the role looks next year with everyone healthy.
Naz Reid is looking like the current choice for 6th Man of the Year as of now. He remains important for Minnesota but there's a chance he gets traded at some point.
Vassell has really struggled recently compared to these last few years. Still has plenty of potential to tap into, but he may be expendable soon.
Watson is a solid all-around player who could be a long-term staple for Denver. He's taken a huge leap over the last few months.
Demin has a lot of fantasy upside when considering his archetype. He's become a really excellent shooter so far, which is crazy to say after what we saw at BYU.
Without Haliburton, Nembhard has had a solid year. He has good role malleability and it's encouraging to see the improvements from 3.
Mitchell remains high and has been very important for this OKC squad. He's a great buy at cost if you think he could take another leap here or elsewhere.
I have a lot of questions about Swain and how his game translates to the NBA in a new role, but the appeal as a do-everything wing/forward is all there.
PJ Washington has been playing well in Dallas. His fit is a bit at odds in Dallas with Cooper Flagg.
It feels like Cason Wallace's fantasy upside is limited, but I still like him enough long-term with his elite defense, especially if he goes elsewhere.
Kristaps Porzingis continues to suffer from POTS and has been in and out of lineups all year for Atlanta and Golden State.
Hart has shot well from 3 this year and continues to deliver on the do-everything role he's made his bread off of.
Ament struggled badly for part of his freshman season, but he's come into his own down the stretch. At cost, he's an interesting investment despite the concern areas.
Kuminga has started to take another step forward being away from Golden State and Steve Kerr. He's playing well for Atlanta.
I think Bilal is done as far as any higher level outcomes, but he's had a good season and has some good role player outcomes here. Still very young.
McCain loses some value on the whole after going to OKC, but he's been playing extremely well with the opportunities given to him so far.
Lively is set to miss the rest of the 2025-2026 season with yet another foot injury. I am out on him ever being a top 75 dynasty asset in his career again.
If you're looking for a ready-to-go rookie with a juicy fantasy profile and tons of skills that NBA teams look for in role players, Yaxel is your man.
Malauch was always going to require patience. If you have him, you need to understand what you signed up for. Some flashes have been interesting so far.
I have some skepticism on Ngongba as a prospect, but the fantasy profile is juicy for the center stuff we like in a shot blocker and rim protector with good touch.
I'm fully expecting LeBron's final year to be this year or next, and by default, his value is pretty much deflated from here. If you have him, you're holding until the end.
Norman Powell has been on a heater this year for Miami in their tinkered offense. He'll be a great name for trivia on random 1x All-Stars.
I'm still in on Christian Braun being a good player once he returns to full-game speed and is healthy. Good time to panic buy.
Bridges' time in Charlotte should be coming to an end as his play has drifted off. His value is likely not all that high elsewhere.
Really like Camara, but the problem areas this year have been strongly felt in the fantasy space.
Unsurprisingly, Ayton has looked better than expected because of Luka and Reaves. Numbers are typical but I don't see a lot of long-term upside still.
More of the same as usual for Rudy Gobert, who delivers on his normal. He's having yet another All-Defense season.
Philon has leveled up this year as a sophomore with Alabama. He has a good guard profile and will be a mid-10s pick in most dynasty drafts as of now.
It's early, but Ty Jerome has been standing out in a huge way for Memphis when healthy.
Nikola Topic has returned from his testicular cancer treatment. He's played very few NBA minutes and is ramping up in the G League. We remain patient with him.
Tyson climbed my boards quick over the last few months. He's having an excellent sophomore season as one of Cleveland's few bright spots for some of this year.
I still really like Santi Aldama, but it's hard to really figure out what Memphis looks like at their best. I think he's a key piece and I like his value at cost.
With Anthony Davis shipped off to Washington, Gafford's place in the rotation is a lot less muddy again.
Statistically, Podz has had a fine, inconsistent year. The conversations on Twitter would make you think it's way worse.
Collins continues to play at his normal pace. He's played well after the Zubac trade but has had some nagging injuries.
Holland is playing a key bench role for Detroit. Still has a lot ways to go but is flashing lots of nice potential at 20.
Gordon has missed some time at different points of the year. Denver has really missed him.
Jaime Jaquez Jr. has had a solid year as he's played a steady role off the bench. His stats have been excellent.
Sorber has a great fantasy profile and has what it takes to be a good starter in OKC. He will miss 2025-2026 with a torn ACL. Good buy-low opportunity for rebuilders.
It's hard to say who actually is the best suited starter is in CHA (or if they are on the roster right now). Still, Moussa is making a strong case against Kalkbrenner.
Sorry if others are significantly higher on KPJ than me, but he is a bad IRL player that is not conducive to winning or positive contributions. Sell him while you can.
Grimes was the big silver lining for Philly after the deadline. He was cooking as a scorer. He signs a qualifying offer with something to prove this year.
Podz has really struggled this year and it feels like the sentiment is that GSW wants him gone at the deadline. I still think there is legit upside here.
Mathurin and Walker deserve way more run than they get with Indiana, and they will get just that this year with the former likely starting at SG next to Nembhard.
Look, I was too high on Monk and dropped him in my ranks, but to go from last year to DNPs in Sacramento is completely unacceptable. What are they doing?
Cam Johnson has taken a step back this year in general and he's trending down on the whole. Still valuable enough for contenders.
Nesmith missed some time this past year and has come back hard with some big games in the playoffs. Very underrated player.
Paul George was already reaching towards the end, but now that he's out for the rest of the fantasy season with a drug suspension, he might be about done.
Risacher's value is crashing hard right now and it remains to be seen if/how he can get it back.
Queta is far from your ideal NBA starting center, but he's looked decent for Boston all things considered. Good fantasy numbers.
Herb is shouldering a ton this year with how poor New Orleans' defense is. Numbers haven't been amazing but should tick up soon.
Christie faded off by the end of the season, and it's fair to question if he can come into next year at a starting level.
Jovic had some hype coming in, but through the first quarter of the season, he's largely regressed from last season.
Filipowski's minutes have been hit or miss, but he's showing he can produce when he gets a large amount. Definite hold/buy still.
Jrue has been crushing it in Portland in a bigger role for the first time in years. He's providing steady value for contenders.
Jase has had some excellent games so far this year. The talent is definitely there even though I still want to see how he keeps it up.
Jimmy Butler suffered a devastating ACL tear this January. He's a psycho and will aim to return, but will he ever be the same player again at age 37?
Simons is mostly just a score-first guard in Boston and I don't expect him to play a strong role on another decent team again.
VanVleet suffered a horribly timed ACL tear. It's fair to question how he recovers from this injury at age 32 as a smaller guard. Him being out is definitely felt so far in HOU.
Clayton has not been heavily involved in the rotation yet, but I'm willing to be patient. I see some high outcomes still.
Ellis finally finds a new home, leaving the worst team in the West to a struggling, yet still-alive, Cavs team. He'll play an important role again.
Thomas is what he is at this point. He's a bucket and can give you plenty of points, but not much else. Very murky future after receiving a qualifying offer from BKN.
How about Dillon Brooks this year? He's having the best scoring stretch of his career and continues to push.
Stewart is having the best year of his career from a fantasy perspective. Still surprisingly very young.
Hunter heads to Sacramento, where his path to good minutes this and next year feels clear. Still, he has become a negative value again very quickly.
A trade elsewhere is what's best for both Detroit and Jaden Ivey, unfortunately. He's struggled badly this year.
Once again, we're seeing Vuc crush for Chicago. He's a solid fantasy player. I would imagine he sticks around with Chicago looking more competent.
Essengue is far from a complete product and has a lot to work on, so it stinks to see him miss the remainder of the year and lose valuable development time.
Wiggins joined the Miami Heat following the Butler trade. He's had a solid fantasy season and should maintain a steady role in Miami as they look to build back up.
Sharpe has been an interesting backup big for a few years now. Not sure why he signed for so cheap to stay in Brooklyn.
Jakucionis had a great game this past week. He's not going to be a consistent player in MIA yet until he earn's Spoelstra trust, but the upside is obvious.
DeRozan gets to reunite with LaVine and will likely finish his career in the next couple years. Still a worthy contender buy for the low if he fits your team.
I've been a longtime Marshall truther and he's been surging recently with the slew of Mavs injuries. I expect him to have a few more prime years like this.
Clifford is an absolute fantasy monster lying in wait as Sacramento flounders around. He'll get his shot soon.
The shooting is still far from ever being close to average, but the playmaking, pace and feel are pretty good for a young guard. How will he, George and Clayton mesh?
Mitchell continues to be very good in Miami. I've had my doubts but he's really revived his career.
With a 3-year deal and him sitting this year out recovering from his Achilles tear, he has a small window of decent play left if he manages to make a full recovery.
Scotty Pippen Jr. is still recovering from toe surgery and yet to make his debut. I think he's very quietly one of MEM's best players.
It doesn't make a lot of sense that Clowney suddenly went from almost out of the NBA to a key floor spacer suddenly, but such is the NBA and development weirdness.
Carter Bryant is a bit of a mystery box in terms of upside. The fantasy game is meh so far but the upside and phyiscal tools are very intriguing.
Hugo has had some massive games this month and is well on his way. He's already a net-positive player for a good team and earning Mazzulla's trust.
Grant is back to his high-scoring output for Portland. I expect he'll garner some trade interest from needy fringe contenders.
I normally try and give some grace to young guards, but the fact that he's not playing with his size, game and with Bones Hyland playing over him scares me.
Wolf has a very appealing fantasy game, but he's not playable at the NBA level yet and has a ways to go. Still definitely worth an investment in dynasty for the long haul.
LaRavia has impressed so far in LA and will continue playing a key starting role this year. Lot to like here as he keeps building chemistry with Luka, Reaves and co.
Dunn has had good moments in Phoenix. He'll be a key piece for them over time with their dire cap situation. Very solid defender despite disappointing numbers this year.
Wiggins continues to play spot roles and when called upon in OKC. Very good player and valuable for his team.
We know who Green is at this point. He'll stick around in GSW until the wheels fall off. His fantasy game isn't what it used to be but he's still a great and valuable player.
It's been great to see Saddiq Bey finally healthy and balling out again. I don't expect this to stick long-term but he is sure to draw some interest at the trade deadline.
Unsurprisingly, Yang hasn't played much and when he has, he's been virtually unplayable. He's going to need time.
Raynaud has been excelling so far with Domantas Sabonis out. He checks all the right boxes. Never should've gone 42nd overall IRL.
Minott has looked solid so far and delivered on the fantasy stuff we hoped he could do in limited minutes in MIN.
Wells has gotten himself out of the slump finally, but the fantasy game is still not all that strong.
Kornet has delivered on top 100 value on the year according to BBM. He's working out great for SA with and without Wemby.
WCJ has had a better year this year and should probably be higher on my ranks, but I still do not have a ton of belief in him at this point.
I fully expect to see Jeremy Sochan on the move at the deadline now that he's been pushed out of the rotation. There may still be some upside here.
What a leap Goga has made when I thought he was close to being out of the league after his time in Indiana. He's become a solid fantasy guy.
Robinson has continually had struggles with staying healthy. If he can't this year, we will likely see him traded.
As usual, Moody has moments of brilliance and struggles, but he's had some of his best this year.
Cam Spencer has ascended up the board with some stellar play over the last month. Is it real with all their injuries?
I love what I've seen from Penda so far and I'm very high on him potentially earning a consistent role next year.
Schroder has been traded once again; this time, he heads to Cleveland to play a bench role behind Donovan Mitchell and Darius Garland.
Cardwell has flashed some interesting stuff for Sacramento at times. He's an old school big with good defensive abilities.
CJ is playing as usual with high scoring outings without a ton else. He's coming up on the end.
Would it shock you that Kyle Kuzma still stinks as a fantasy player in Milwaukee? It shouldn't after his terrible playoff stretch.
As expected, Sexton is mostly a 6th man with some occasional spot starts. Still a good scorer but his best days are now behind him.
I've been a big Ayo fan for a while and I think he deserves better than Chicago. One of the more underrated players out there.
Holmes has yet to play much in the NBA. With Jonas as their backup, this gives Holmes more time to get fresh and get ready for a bigger role next year.
This year is now Rui's second in a row where he's shooting over 50% from the field and 40% from 3 on at least 1 per game.
Harris is still playing a steady role in Detroit with a lot less reliance on his scoring. He's coming towards the end.
Allen is having his best year and popping off for Phoenix with their need for scorers. What him and Brooks is doing is pretty fake without Jalen Green, but still notable.
Not much more upside for the Magic to extract from Da Silva, but as a rotation player, I think he's good and should have a 10+ year career in the NBA.
McBride is a dawg and is suited to play big minutes on a funky Knicks bench. Not a ton of strong upside besides what he gets in big minutes.
Sam Hauser doesn't have much true upside, but he is a good 3&D player and can pop off for 9 3s now and again. He will cook for Boston this year for sure.
Caruso in OKC is making for some terrifying defense. He's a winning player, but spending the remainder of his prime on a deep contender is not A+ for fantasy.
Dort is a crucial piece to OKC as a defender and shooter. There's no big upside from here, but he's still pretty young and will remain a staple on this team.
Richard stays high on my board for the impact he's been making on GSW as a rookie. Really like him moving forward.
Huff is a really underrated rotation guy who has shown a lot of promise for fantasy this season. Indiana scooped him up as a possible starter. Lot of potential here.
Gillespie inked a one-year deal to stick with the Suns this year. They lack true PG options, so he will play at least a little.
Shead is still playing a small rotation well for Toronto and it's telling that he's still been given work even with how loaded they are. Good assists guy this deep.
Russ went from almost being done as an NBA player to being the starter in Sacramento. It is Sacramento, but he does look revitalized on a bad team like this.
Keldon Johnson isn't a great fantasy player, but he has posted excellent value this year and feels much more defined in a role.
Hendricks has struggled to earn minutes consistently. I think we can probably put this one to bed but there is still some hope if he can get there this year.
Brandon Williams is on track to go from Silly Season star to legitimate role player for Dallas until Kyrie is healthy. Him and Ryan Nembhard will compete for minutes.
I like Toppin as a rotation player. I don't think he's ever a full-time starter on a good team, but he does a lot of winning stuff for the Pacers in less minutes.
AJ Green's role has expanded over the years, and hopefully, you aren't surprised that he's still shooting over 40% from 3 on higher volume. He's like that.
Merrill is such a pure shooter and his shot is one of the cleanest I've ever seen. He will be one of a few guys working to replace Ty Jerome off the bench.
There's a lot to like about Drake Powell with his athleticism and tools from North Carolina. There's a small chance he's Brooklyn's best player from this class.
Kris Dunn is a solid rotation defender for LAC. Not much upside here but he's a good player and will stick around a little longer.
Walsh is still young and needs some time, but the upside is still there in his physical tools. Curious if he can carve out anything in Year 3 and a lost year for the team.
Traore has struggled early and clearly needs a lot of time to develop. He's been sent to the G League but Brooklyn really needs to give him real NBA minutes soon.
We should've seen this coming. Nembhard has been playing a real role and is playing well. Will continue to monitor and see if he can keep this up.
Krejci has been one of the more underrated role players in the NBA this year. I think the trade to Portland helps his fantasy value.
Missi has started to get pushed out of NOLA's rotation after an intriguing rookie year. There is some hope if he's traded.
We've seen Champagnie have some solid moments, but the previous overreliance on starting him is a sign he's probably best as a rotation player.
Jenkins is set to get a hefty payday this offseason if he does ultimately turn down standard deals from Detroit. He truly is the answer for the long-term backup PG role.
Despite Walker Kessler going down, Nurkic has been playing with a little gas left in the tank. Not expecting much after this season.
There's something there with Gueye, and you see it all over the tape. I think he's got some intriguing upside that is worth buying on now.
What's this? Tidjane Salaun starting to look like an actual NBA player? I'm still not holding out a lot of hope but we'll see where things go...
We know what Oubre is and what his game looks like. He's a bucket but doesn't offer a ton of strong fantasy appeal besides that.
Melton heads back to GSW and signs a deal following the Kuminga resolution. Could be a bit of a sneaky buy.
It's getting close to over for Bub after the Wizards traded for Trae Young. He's going to need a huge blow-up ROS to save things for himself.
Huerter has quietly been really good this season and made some real returns to his best years.
We haven't seen a lot of Fleming just yet, but I anticipate he will get more opportunities over the next few months.
McNeeley cracks the first round in a good situation in Charlotte. The fantasy game isn't amazing yet but he could really be maximized here.
Jones chose to stay in Chicago with a new deal and has been killing it so far. Huge riser out of nowhere.
I'm closely watching Asa Newell after some fiery games when he gets real minutes. Holding tight and buying if I can.
Brown has not been as good as I'd hoped returning to Denver, but he's at least playing a role again and might earn more burn as the year goes on.
Alvarado has good fantasy value for his minutes, but there's just not much upside for him unless there are injuries. There's a chance a trade lets him see more opportunity.
Carter has struggled to get it going in NBA minutes since making his debut earlier in 2025. He'll need a little refining but the fantasy upside is still there.
McConnell is one of the better, more consistently underrated bench players in the NBA. He fits the Pacers perfectly.
There's some real upside with Post that Golden State could tap into. He's a good rotation piece and able to produce in limited minutes.
Portis has dropped off the map a little this year and it remains to be seen if he'll tick back up into a more normal role for him.
The offense remains a work in progress, but if you want to bet on the tools, athleticism, and two-way appeal, Thiero has a lot to love.
Gradey Dick needs a trade to salvage his career at this point. He's just continued to struggle for Toronto.
Mamu set an NBA record 34 points in 19 minutes. What can he do with the possibility of more run in Toronto? Time will tell.
Valančiūnas has looked pretty steady as Sabonis' backup and the most competent of his time in Sacramento by far.
Still crazy to think Royce O'Neale cost the Suns a first round pick with their current state of things. Good role player in general.
I'm anticipating another trade for the Wizards at some point and Kispert's name is sure to draw a little interest. Not sure what to expect moving forward.
Will Riley in Washington makes total sense when you look at what they value. I don't expect him to play a lot this year.
Bona appears to be a current lock for Philadelphia's primary backup to Joel Embiid. He's looked sharp since early 2025.
I expected much more from Furphy so far this year. I'm not giving up on him, but it is still concerning we've
Kolek bag holders, take a lap. He's finally starting to figure it out and build on some good games over the last month.
Smith is just a backup big at this point and does not carry much value, but if Vucevic is traded, he could be a Silly Season hero.
Standard 3PT specialist stuff. We know what it is with Duncan Robinson. He's played well so far this year.
After this year's terrible stint and a hip injury that knocks Beal out for the season, he may be cooked.
The fit couldn't be better in Indiana and Kam is absolutely going to get opportunities to play. He's been out for the start of the season.
Walker has been terrible this year despite plenty of open opportunities. He's likely traded at the deadline and could be an interesting 2nd team breakout guy.
IJax has been playable this year recovering from his Achilles tear, but the fantasy game has not been impressive save for a few games.
Whitmore fell out of favor in WAS and was diagnosed with DVT. Nowadays, this is not a big concern, but it is still worth noting that it could impact his career.
Beasley is reportedly set to sign with a team pretty soon while still being under investigation by the NBA for the gambling allegations.
Vince has underwhelmed again this year. Cedric Coward and other guys have surpassed him.
I'm not overwhelmingly confident that Ben Saraf will evolve into a good shooter long-term, but there is a lot to like as a big guard.
Landale sticks around in the NBA as he signs a one-year deal with the Memphis Grizzlies. Not expecting anything but emergency depth at this rate.
Julian's brother has been excellent with the Wizards this season. Really impressed by his hard work in securing a full-time NBA role.
Lonzo Ball has been a bit of a trainwreck statistically this year. His inconsistency with CLE has hurt them. Still somehow within the top 220 per game according to BBM.
DLo is on what might be his last chance to keep the career and name recognition standing. He took a 2-year, $12M deal with Dallas.
For what it's worth, GTJ is shooting over 40% from 3 and continues to do that well. He's doing quite well for making pennies relative to other NBA vets.
Bogi shook the rust off recently and looked good for the Clippers post-deadline. Beal coming in may hurt his opportunities but returning to 6MOY is not impossible.
LeVert gets buckets and did just that for Atlanta. I'm curious how he fares for Detroit and what his role can look like.
Timelord has been playing a little more recently, but by and large, he's unable to play large chunks of minutes due to his injury.
DJJ has quietly been having the best year of his career before he went down with an injury in November. Expecting more of that once he's back.
Middleton is reaching the end of his career. I expect him to be used as trade filler at the deadline or a possible buyout candidate for one last ride for a championship.
Nothing Mann is doing is all that "real", but he is proving some value to Brooklyn and fantasy managers in deep leagues.
What in the world happened with Yabusele this year after a big breakout season in Philadelphia?
Charlotte has found a potential multi-year role player in Sion James who can play lots of minutes, but he's not posting much statistically.
Despite having a good rookie season, Edwards has largely been on the outside looking in this year.
Proctor is waiting behind Craig Porter Jr. for NBA minutes. Likely won't happen for him this year unless there's injuries.
Watford truthers, we are so back! Watford signed a 2-year deal with the 76ers and with Guerschon Yabusele gone, Watford could be an intriguing replacement option.
Strus apparently still has a long recovery ahead of him with no timetable on his foot. We'll see what happens with him.
Anthony got flipped to Memphis and then bought out. He has a real opportunity available in Milwaukee. He just needs to beat out Kevin Porter Jr. and Ryan Rollins.
I'm very high on Jaylen Clark's future. He's looked excellent in MIN's rotation and the fact that a stickler like HC Chris Finch trusts him is reason enough to buy in early.
Mann re-signed as expected with Charlotte but feels a little buried with Collin Sexton and other guards in the mix.
Larsson is kind of a jack of all trades/master of none rotation piece. Don't see a lot of upside for him but feels like he could stick around and earn a role in MIA.
Scheierman's role remains very low with little to do. I expected way better out of him this year.
GG Jackson is approaching a massive low point as he sits outside the Grizzlies' rotation. He's still extremely young and has upside to tap into.
CPJ is actually one of the more interesting role players out there that could be a hit if Cleveland's bench wasn't so deep. Worth a watch to see what happens.
Horford is somehow still kicking and delivering on top 200 per game value. He'll turn 40 if/when the Warriors make the playoffs.
I always liked Ben Sheppard, but he's been really bad this year. Hoping he bounces back later in the year.
Broome has an appealing fantasy game that should pop with his playmaking, but it appears that Bona and Drummond are the primary backups for now.
JWill probably deserves to be higher than this because he's legitimately solid as a rotation piece, but it's hard to trust he has a role of much size at all.
Barnes still has some juice even in San Antonio. We know what he is as a boring starter who can pop on occasion.
Cody Williams is still struggling to earn real minutes with the Jazz. It might already be over but we'll see how this year goes for any signs of hope.
PatWill robbed the Bulls blind on that contract. He looked surprisingly playable this year early but settles back into his normal self.
I don't know how he does it, but Andre Drummond continues to survive and deliver some quality play in philly.
Adams continues to play a small rotation role for Houston. He was a major playoff weapon last year and I expect a few big games based on the opponent this year.
Small's fantasy game has continued to pop when he plays for Memphis. Could be a real sleeper hit for deeper leagues here.
Richards is rumored to be a lower value trade target with teams in need of a center. He's not very good but he's got some fantasy juice.
DFS is who he is, and that constitutes a good starter/high-minute rotation guy that's better IRL than for fantasy. He's expected to make his debut soon.
Hawkins is mostly just a 3PT specialist and nothing more. He's mainly just a rotation piece at this point.
I don't really expect Barnhizer to play much with how deep this roster is but the fantasy profile is intriguing. He's been killing it in the G League so far.
Knecht hasn't wowed much aside from a few big pops. It's to be expected for the archetype. Not sure how much higher the upside is at this rate.
THJ was left off of the last update due to error, but he's back now and playing a real role for the Nuggets.
Ziaire Williams has been an interesting discovery by the Nets after he didn't work out in Brooklyn. Not expecting much after this season.
As usual, Vukcevic continues to tease good fantasy play here and there. He deserves a way more consistent role.
Bones has been playing legit minutes with Minnesota this year over Rob Dillingham. Still not sure he's all that good, but he is reviving his career in a big way.
Mogbo has still yet to do much this year. I still have some hope for him but the better version of him (Collin Murray-Boyles) is the priority.
Agbaji might sink more into the rotation with their additions and everyone healthy this year. Not expecting much from him. Very boring fantasy player.
Brandon Clarke has once again suffered a calf injury and will miss at least 3 weeks. He may never be fully healthy again, unfortunately.
Tyus Jones has been downright awful this year. It's possible that this is his last year in the NBA as a full-time player.
Strawther has basically fallen out of the Nuggets' rotation and remains to be seen if he returns.
We're unlikely to see Cisse get much mileage until one of their centers is traded, but keep an eye on him. Fantastic per-minute stuff and the advanced numbers like him.
Garza has been playing a backup role to Queta in Boston. He's far from ideal but playing fine enough.
Okoro is what he is at this stage in his career. Chicago will use him some but don't expect anything for fantasy.
Thybulle was MIA essentially all year. Let's hope we see him soon and return to form as a strong defender this next year.
Brook Lopez is coming up on the end of his career. He's been brutally bad for fantasy this year.
It's been an unusual year for Buddy, who is having his worst 3PT shooting season ever so far. He may be close to the end.
I like Simone as a rotation shooter. I could easily see him looking really good for Miami and could get a legit role with Haywood Highsmith out to open the season.
Vanderbilt is a way better IRL player than fantasy, and even then, he's not doing much on either front.
One thing about BBall Paul? He's always going to have some random explosions per year and he's had a few for Detroit already.
Klay's value is really only in the name at this point. He's about done after this year, I'd imagine.
Mo Wagner was done for the season after an ACL tear. We should expect him to make a full recovery and return to form in Orlando this summer.
AJ Johnson still has talent to tap into, but he's barely played aside from blowouts or miniscule stretches.
Kelly Olynyk used to command tanks, but he may be done doing that in San Antonio with Wemby leading the competitive Spurs.
Spencer Jones' fantasy output has been very inconsistent, but hs's playing a lot of minutes right now. Continuing to monitor him.
TJD is still playing very small, insignificant minutes for the Warriors despite doing well as a rookie.
Sanders has been playing real minutes for the Clippers so far and has flashed some fantasy appeal.
We're approaching the end for Mike Conley. He's starting to be phased out at large despite some good games and shooting over 40% from 3.
Tomlin really impressed me at Summer League and is starting to break into CLE's rotation a bit. Keep an eye on him.
I love the potential Watkins has in Washington. The defensive numbers translating from Summer League would be extremely exciting.
An interesting observation: John Tonje is currently averaging 50/40/90 splits on 17.1 PPG in the G League. Keep a very close eye on him.
Amari Williams has been playing real well in the G League so far. He's currently averaging 5.2 assists in 29.3 minutes.
It's been a struggle for Isaac this year, who is barely seeing the floor. I'd imagine he's fodder for trades down the stretch.
Rocco needs a ton of time to keep developing, but early G League returns have been pretty good so far.
I expect Highsmith to be a potential cheap trade target for a contender as Brooklyn looks to liquidate veterans again.
I like Karlo Matkovic and thought earning a real role was a possibility, but Troy Weaver cooked any chances of that by now.
Josh Green has been incredibly underwhelming in Charlotte and just seems like a cardio role player. I question whether him or Sion James are better going forward.
My sentiment that Walter is of little interest to me for fantasy remains the case - but he has had good NBA looks when the 3PT shot can fall.
Wade was a great undrafted gem for the Cavs and plays a steady bench role. Really good IRL player but essentially a cardio guy for fantasy purposes.
To me, Kennard is emblematic of a better IRL than fantasy guy. How much can he contribute this season for the Hawks?
Both these Spencer brothers can really hoop! Pat has had some massive games for the Warriors this year.
Simpson has continued to play a good chunk of minutes, but the fantasy game is not all that strong.
We know what Clarkson is by now: rough 9Cat player but money for points leagues. Should play a real role in NYK.
Bagley will forever be known as the guy drafted before Luka Doncic. He's still not very good but he's doing a little for the Wizards still.
Capela's reign in Atlanta ends and he returns to Houston on a contract that feels primed for trade filler if he doesn't play much.
I'm very skeptical of YKN and knowing that LAC has burned fantasy owners before by not playing their youngsters makes me want to avoid Niederhauser.
Dadiet is a great investment for a multi-year rebuild. Could he be a good piece in a few years if the Knicks get priced out of bench guys?
One of the brothers of Jrue Holiday. Actually still decent when he does get the minutes here and there.
Wesley has failed to do much of anything at the NBA level to date, and he ends up in Portland to ride the bench.
Miller still has a ways to go to be a full-time NBA guy. It's shocking how terrible his defense is for his size and physical traits. It'll take a trade to jumpstart things.
Martin has stuck around in Brooklyn and keeps playing a role (for some reason). Good very deep league end of bench guy.
Koby Brea might be a role player that can't do a ton offensively, but he more than makes up for it as a pure 3PT specialist who's shot 43.4% from 3 in his CBB career.
Troy Weaver and his fetish for centers brought Kevon Looney into town. Don't know how much he plays alongside Queen, Missi and others.
Ighodaro may play some spot minutes here and there, with Phoenix added two centers this offseason. I don't see Oso making a big case moving forward.
Most of us knew that Hayes isn't really an NBA-caliber player and stunk in the playoffs. The Lakers will replace him as a starter with Ayton.
Howard's still been inconsistent, but when the shot falls, it looks very good. He barely played last season and will be looking for a role this season.
I still buy Tyler Smith's upside. Milwaukee has almost no real young NBA up and comers with potential on the roster past him.
Barlow returns to my ranks again. He's playing occasional minutes for Philly but I don't see much long-term upside as a full-time NBA player.
Svi has not only been servicable for Utah this year but also looked better than average.
I think there's a real possibility Kris Murray might not stick in the NBA. Portland was the wrong place for him. He's struggled to shoot from 3.
Collins has had some fine fantasy play in the past few years, but he's about done once his contract is up next summer.
Martin is smaller and lacks high-end skills, but his energy and pure athleticism is solid. He's playing well for the 905 Raptors right now.
Peavy has the size, potential shooting, and fundamental skills to overcome limitations. Could be an intriguing sleeper depending on if NOLA has injuries
It's about over for CP3 at this point. He's playing very few minutes in LAC and is now waived.
Dieng is surely getting traded to a rebuilder at the deadline. I'm interested if he could be a second team revival guy.
We know what it is with GP2 at this point. Solid IRL rotation guy but he can't do much of anything for fantasy aside from the steals.
PJ Hall has bounced from the Hornets to Grizzlies and come back to the Hornets this week. Still hoping he could emerge at some point.
Bronny has not played much this year to the surprise of almost no one. Still might be worth watching.
Grant Williams tore his ACL this past year and is expected to make a full recovery. He's not a priority piece, but he might play more than we think this year.
Caleb Martin has barely played and been bad when he has for Dallas. Meanwhile, Quentin Grimes has looked very, very good. Another masterful gambit, Nico Harrison.
Plumlee is still chugging along and might actually end up starting in Charlotte come opening night. Wild to say that in 2025.
Okogie's fine for what he is as a defensive-minded wing in low minutes. He's a vet minimum player without much fantasy upside.
Sims is just an athlete and nothing more. Great bounce but not much skill. The Bucks are pretty rough depth wise, so maybe he gets some real looks this year.
Pretty average rotation guy in general, but Prince gets good minutes in Milwaukee due to their bench. He's a good value this deep.
Pickett seemed to figure some things out at points this year. I don't think he's going to play a ton this year and I'm curious what he does with Bruce Brown here.
Kind of amazed that Jalen Wilson has made it this long in the NBA - AND done a great job as a role player.
Hukporti is just emergency depth right now without a whole lot of upside. I'm concerned about his lower body holding up.
Lanier is a pretty meh fantasy player for me. Mostly will just be shooting 3s and not much else. He'll be a better IRL player than a fantasy player.
Hardy stuck around in Dallas on a cheap 3-year deal this past summer. He's a strong scorer with very little else to offer. He's like Cam Thomas (derogatory).
Bufkin has floated around the league so far. He's now in Brooklyn after bouncing around the Grizzlies and Lakers after the Nets cut him once.
Maybe Johnson can still be something in Miami. Never fully count out an undrafted guy on an Erik Spoelstra-led team.
Achiuwa is struggling to make it in the NBA. He's currently with Sacramento but already bounced around multiple teams this season.
Not sure if Rupert is ever going to be a full-time NBA player, but he was really sharp this summer and has always shown flashes.
We hoped Reath would be traded, but no such luck. We need to hope he can find a new home to unlock the potential.
Kenny Hustle plays a good low-minute role on OKC and does a nice job with the opportunity. He's not a very strong fantasy player but he can do a bit of everything.
Jordan Miller is a downright Summer League superstar. Can he secure some real/consistent NBA minutes at some point? He needs to leave the Clippers.
Simmons is still a free agent. No idea where he ultimately signs, but I think it feels clear that we're never getting the return of a fantasy superstar.
Goodwin has had some nice moments over the year and continues to look interesting for a deep bench guy.
Tillman has some experience with Mazzulla and their center depth is bad. He might get some run but I'm not expecting much.
Thomas Bryant has been playing spot big minutes for the Cavs this year. Not a very good player but he can get the stats flowing sometimes.
Niang is still out due to a foot injury. We're waiting on some news to see if he'll be back soon. He could be a tanking production guy.
It's really odd to me that Jabari Walker couldn't get a real contract this offseason. Still, I like the chance he has to push for a role in Philly. Think he's solid as a role player.
Nance returns to Cleveland to the excitement of Cavs fans everywhere. They finally have a third big to lean on if Mobley and Allen are hurt.
Terry hasn't done much to really excite at the NBA level. He's just not been able to contribute much of anything even in a rebuild.
Battle is quite good for an undrafted free agent. I doubt he's much more than a deep bench shooter for his career.
Plain and simple: I don't think Sasser has it as an NBA player. He can be a good scorer, but he can't do much else and he's small.
SloMo's not very good for fantasy at this point. Hard to see a strong path to minutes for him for the long haul.
Dru Smith has looked OK in limited moments for the Heat. Not expecting much of a role moving forward.
Konchar is a fun role player when he gets looks, but he's really just filler for Memphis at this point for trades. I'm always hopeful seeing him get looks for emergency depth.
A former Euroleague MVP returns to the NBA with a much-improved game and a wide-open shot on the Suns. Don't expect a Yabu-like year but could be interesting.
Toohey has been waived by the Warriors following the announcement he would be out for the season. Still think there's an NBA player here.
Dillon Jones has been waived and traded in the G League so many times that it's hard to keep track.
Kevin Love is well out of his prime and will keep on trucking with Utah until his contract is up.
Bouyea has played limited minutes for the Suns and had a few moments here and there.
Boucher is still trucking with BOS, but opportunities have been far and few between so far.
I understand people being higher on Smith for his good streak with all the injuries, but I'm not all that convinced. He signed a two-way deal with the Lakers.
Chicago isn't exactly deep with talent at center, and with Olbrich coming right over to the league, he could earn a role in the long haul. He's got good touch around the rim.
Wallace has found a niche in Atlanta in their deep rotation. Fun player but doesn't get many opportunities.
Bogo is about 2-3 years away from being an NBA player and will stay overseas as a stash, so I don't see him being worth an early 2nd round pick in rookie drafts at all.
Batum is near the end of his career and only of real value to deep-league contenders. We know what he's all about.
I don't know what the future is for Keon Johnson with the Nets with their recent additions. He has looked like an OK player for stretches.
Juzang is a ridiculous hooper. He's managed to hang around for a bit and I think he will continue to do so.
Phillips has some juice to be a real NBA player at some point. He's got some athletic pop, he can rebound, he can defend well, but he's not a shooter.
Branham is still young, but I think he's unfortunately just a bust that won't stick around in the NBA much longer.
The thing about Isaac Jones is he just can't shoot 3s, but he was dominant at Summer League and one of the best players out there. Is any of this possibly real?
Djurisic is still a ways away from ever contributing in the NBA unless he can shoot it, but he showed some good ballhandling chops this summer.
Taelon Peter is a statistically elite sharpshooter from range and could have some very under-the-radar upside on a team without a lot to play for this year.
Gabe Vincent was downright terrible for the Lakers last season when he did play, which wasn't much. This season, he seems to be figuring things out.
It remains to be seen if and when Nunez ever comes over. He has had some concerning knee injuries recently that I'm keeping an eye on.
Carlson has had a great start to his NBA career with a bunch of 10-day contract stints. I think he'll hang around the NBA for a while.
OMax has surprised us in actually getting reps this year after largely underwhelming. I don't think he's an NBA player, unfortunately.
Coffey has had some genuinely good moments in the NBA before, but he's just an emergency depth guy for Milwaukee at this point.
Bobi has some interesting fantasy flashes with his passing touch, but I just don't think he has the juice to be an NBA difference-maker.
The younger brother of Max Christie, and unfortunately, he plays in the LA team that refuses to play their young talent.
Houstan could have a sudden shot at earning a role in Orlando. I'm not all that confident at this point but when teams lose depth, anything is worth looking at.
Injuries have derailed Exum last year and this year as he undergoes knee surgery. This could be the end of a nice NBA resurgence.
One of the more underdiscussed Warriors storylines is that Santos has found his way into the rotation and had some good looks. Interesting hold going into next season.
Andre Jackson Jr. is a back-end rotation guy and nothing more at this point. Good defender and passer but a bad scorer.
Bol Bol remains unsigned and gets to keep hanging with Carti and getting fits off. He might be better at that than basketball at this point.
